rubrics.justification: The response gives a plausible general blastocyst assessment but appears to undercall the reported hatching status and questions the AA features despite the lab grade. It avoids major fabrication, yet the image-based morphology discussion is somewhat uncertain and not tightly matched to the provided 4AA/hatching description.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, semen, endometrium, and prior losses well, and appropriately frames prior miscarriage/biochemical pregnancy as the main caution despite favorable baseline prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent: favorable age and embryo quality increase prognosis, while prior losses temper confidence. Minor tension exists between calling the embryo less than textbook 4AA and still assigning a relatively high implantation range.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based: single embryo transfer, standard luteal support, avoidance of unproven add-ons, and RPL/uterine evaluation if losses continue. The PGT-A discussion is appropriately cautious for age 31, though some suggestions are somewhat generalized.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, monitoring, uterine cavity review, endocrine/metabolic checks, and RPL workup if needed. Useful and clinically relevant, though not highly protocol-specific.
